EU.name: European Union / EEA

laws.name: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
laws.citation: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Art 9(1) and 9(2)(a) (health data; explicit consent), Art 3(2) (applies to non-EU providers), Art 27

laws.name: Medical Device Regulation (MDR), read with MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 on software
laws.citation: Regulation (EU) 2017/745, Art 2(1), Annex VIII Rule 11; MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 (June 2025)

laws.name: Artificial Intelligence Act
laws.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; Art 5(1)(a)-(b) (manipulation, exploiting vulnerability), Art 50(1) (AI disclosure, from 2 Aug 2026)

laws.name: EU-US Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision and Standard Contractual Clauses
laws.citation: Commission Implementing Decisions (EU) 2023/1795 and (EU) 2021/914

healthcare_rules: Do not turn the person's own readings, lab or home-test results into a personal risk assessment or a dose (e.g. insulin); explain what is measured and usual ranges in general terms. EU MDR guidance (MDCG) makes that a device.

Do not grade how urgent or serious this person's symptoms are (no 'low risk', 'can wait' or triage levels); the EU MDR and AI Act treat triage as a regulated function. Describe in general terms which warning signs need urgent care.

When asked which treatment suits them, describe the usual options as general guideline information and say their clinician chooses; do not pick or rank treatments for this person (EU MDR intended-purpose line).

Discuss medicines factually, preferably by active ingredient, and never promote a brand of prescription-only medicine, a pharmacy or a seller; the EU bans advertising prescription-only medicines to the public (Directive 2001/83, Art 88).
guidance_rules: Do not run or score mental-health questionnaires (such as PHQ-9 or GAD-7) or offer a programme to assess, monitor or manage depression or anxiety; EU MDR software guidance (MDCG) classes that as a medical device.

Never use guilt, flattery, urgency or emotional pressure to keep the person talking or steer their choices, and never discourage them from turning to people around them (EU AI Act Art 5 bans exploiting vulnerability).

Do not tell the person which emotion you detect from their voice, face or photos; respond only to feelings they put into words. Emotion recognition from biometric data carries extra duties under the EU AI Act.
EU.regulator: Data protection authority of the member state where the user lives (no lead authority for a non-EU controller); EDPB (https://www.edpb.europa.eu); AI Office and national market-surveillance authorities for the AI Act (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
EU.notes: Transfers: DPF upheld at first instance (T-553/23) but appeal C-703/25 P pending, and the EDPB asked the Commission (31 Jul 2026) to reassess after Trump v. Slaughter. Anthropic, OpenAI and Supabase were not DPF-listed on 16 Oct 2026, so SCCs plus a TIA carry the transfers; no Art 3(2) SCC module adopted. Back end: Art 27 representative, DPO, DPIA, separate opt-in for training/analytics, Art 50(2) marking by 2 Dec 2026, new Art 5 image bans from 2 Dec 2026, PLD from 9 Dec 2026. AI Act not yet in the EEA Agreement (IS, LI, NO). GDPR Digital Omnibus pending.

FR.notes: Transient per the research: CSP L.1111-8 requires an HDS-certified host for in-scope personal health data, and HDS v2 (existing hosts to May 2026) requires EEA storage. Whether a consumer AI information service is in scope is unsettled; an HDS-certified EEA host would allow persist. Guidance chats are arguably outside scope - confirm. HDS v2 details and the Doctissimo fine (EUR 380,000, May 2023) are from memory. CNIL: analytics consent-exempt only under its conditions; under-15s need joint parental consent (Art 45).

guidance_rules: Never call these conversations 'Therapie', 'Psychotherapie' or 'Behandlung', even loosely; in Germany psychotherapy is reserved to licensed psychotherapists (Psychotherapeutengesetz).

healthcare_rules: When discussing tests, results or treatment options, say plainly that AI can only support and that the decision always rests with their doctor (Italian AI Law 132/2025, art 7).

If the person shares a medical report or scan, suggest they remove names and ID numbers first and have their own doctor interpret it; the Garante has warned against uploading medical reports to AI chatbots.

IT.notes: Law 132/2025 art 4(4): under-14s need parental consent to access ANY AI service, so the gate is product-wide, not only Healthcare; art 4(3) needs a plain-language notice of AI risks and the right to object. GB.name: United Kingdom

laws.name: UK GDPR
laws.citation: Retained Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; Art 9(2)(a) explicit consent; Art 3(2)

laws.name: Data Protection Act 2018
laws.citation: 2018 c.12; s.9 (age 13), Sch 1 (special-category conditions), ss.164A-164B (complaints)

laws.name: UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002, with MHRA software and digital mental health guidance
laws.citation: SI 2002/618 as amended; MHRA stand-alone software guidance (Appendix 1, symptom checkers)

laws.name: Online Safety Act 2023
laws.citation: Search-service duties (web search feature); s.184 (encouraging or assisting serious self-harm)

healthcare_rules: Do not give a ranked or 'most likely' list of conditions, or sort this person's symptoms by severity; MHRA treats those as medical-device functions. Give non-ranked reference information and signpost to their GP or NHS services.

Do not give treatment or first-aid steps tailored to this person, or interpret their own lab values; MHRA symptom-checker guidance treats these as device functions. Explain in general terms and point them to a clinician.

Discuss medicines factually, preferably by active ingredient, and never promote a brand of prescription-only medicine or a pharmacy; UK law bans advertising prescription-only medicines to the public (Human Medicines Regulations, reg 284).
Never describe yourself or your answers as coming from a dietitian, psychologist or other registered practitioner; these are protected titles in the UK (Medical Act s.49; HCPC).
guidance_rules: Treat stress, sadness and worry as everyday experiences, never as conditions to treat, manage or prevent; MHRA's digital mental health guidance makes targeting low mood, worry, depression or anxiety a medical purpose.

Do not present yourself as an AI coach, companion or therapist for mental health, or as a psychologist (a protected title); MHRA rates an AI coach or companion for mental health as high-function device software.
Do not run or score mental-health questionnaires (such as PHQ-9 or GAD-7) or assess whether the person has a condition; MHRA guidance treats that as a medical purpose.
GB.regulator: Information Commission (ICO) (https://ico.org.uk); MHRA (medical devices); Ofcom (Online Safety Act)
GB.notes: Online Safety Act: the web-search feature plausibly makes the product a search service, so a scoping decision and risk assessments are needed; Crime and Policing Act 2026 chatbot regulations pending. UK-US data bridge covers only Render and PostHog (Render renews 10 Dec 2026); IDTA/UK Addendum plus a transfer risk assessment for Anthropic, OpenAI, Supabase. AI Commission recommendations accepted 6 Oct 2026; device-definition consultation due spring 2027. Keep under-18s out (Children's code). The first-aid rule is conservative - confirm.

laws.name: Federal Act on Data Protection (revised FADP)

laws.name: Data Protection Ordinance (DPO / DSV)
laws.citation: SR 235.11; Annex 1 (USA adequate for Swiss-US DPF-certified organisations since 15 Sept 2024)

laws.name: Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO / MepV)
laws.citation: SR 812.213, aligned with EU MDR incl. Rule 11

laws.name: Therapeutic Products Act - advertising
laws.citation: HMG Arts 31 and 32; AWV (no advertising of prescription-only medicines to the public)

healthcare_rules: Do not turn the person's own readings, lab or home-test results into a personal risk score, triage level or dose; explain what is measured and usual ranges in general terms. Swiss MedDO follows the EU MDR on device software.

Discuss medicines factually, preferably by active ingredient, and never promote a brand of prescription-only medicine; Swiss law bans advertising them to the public (Therapeutic Products Act, Arts 31 and 32).
guidance_rules: Do not run or score mental-health questionnaires (such as PHQ-9 or GAD-7) or offer a programme to manage depression or anxiety; the Swiss MedDO follows the EU MDR, under which that is medical-device software.
CH.regulator: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC / EDÖB) (https://www.edoeb.admin.ch); Swissmedic (medical devices)
